neural_bridge_note: Per AIWorkHub neural-control-first doctrine, future SELECTION of adapter/runner/topic (which agent to launch for which task) must be a LEARNED routing decision, not a regex/keyword cue router. This design deliberately adds NO cue router and NO runtime keyword branch: adapter availability is a read-only presence probe and routing is a static human-configured allowlist + explicit safety gates only. The intelligence layer (learned launch/route/abstain policy) is deferred to trainable targets — curriculum rows and an explicit MCP_NEURAL_LAUNCH_ROUTING_MIGRATION_V1 task card — so no hidden regex/table cognition is introduced as launch authority.

phases.deliverable: A read-only MCP tool that returns the exact argv it WOULD run, the resolved adapter, runner/topic, cwd pin, and a collision-guard preflight result — but executes nothing. Plan-only is the default and only behaviour in this phase.

phases.deliverable: Data model + persistence schema for launch requests and their lifecycle states (queued, planned, blocked_launch_disabled, would_run, terminal). No real agent process is ever spawned; every request terminates in 'blocked_launch_disabled' while ALLOW_LAUNCH!=1. State-machine transitions are pure data.
phases.exit_gate: State model round-trips through persistence; with ALLOW_LAUNCH unset every request lands in blocked_launch_disabled; no os.fork/subprocess/os.exec* for an agent proc; audit log records each state transition.
phases.title: Launch queue + process-state model (still disabled)

phases.deliverable: Wire the AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_LAUNCH gate mirroring the ALLOW_WRITES write-gate. A real launch is permitted ONLY when ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 AND ALLOW_WRITES=1 AND every safety_gate passes (allowlist, collision preflight, cwd/env sandbox, concurrency cap, audit). Default stays fully disabled; dry-run remains the default action.
phases.exit_gate: Launch path unreachable unless ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 AND ALLOW_WRITES=1 AND all of write_gate_parity, runner_topic_allowlist, audit_log, collision_guard_preflight, dry_run_default, cwd_process_sandbox_pin, concurrency_cap pass; blocked attempts audited; rollback = unset ALLOW_LAUNCH restores disabled default.
phases.title: Gated enablement (only phase that can ever launch)

safety_gates.requirement: A launch requires AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 AND AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES=1; both default '0'. Mirrors core.writes_allowed() / run_taskctl write-gate exactly.
Only runner/topic pairs on an explicit static allowlist may be launched; any unknown or off-topic pair is blocked and audited.
Every launch, plan, and blocked attempt appends one entry to the append-only audit.jsonl (reuse core.write_audit_entry); env values/secrets are never logged.
taskctl collision-guard must pass immediately before a launch is permitted; any stale/conflicting claim blocks the launch.
Plan-only (dry-run) is the default action; a real launch requires an explicit opt-in argument beyond the gate flags, never the default code path.
Any launched process has cwd pinned to AIWORKHUB_REPO, a scrubbed env (no secret vars), argv-list only (no shell=True), and bounded timeout; no arbitrary command execution.
A small concurrency cap (default 1) limits simultaneously launched agents; exceeding the cap blocks new launches to protect the workstation and the shared task queue.
